title: Briefing: Italy, South Africa, India, Albania, Canada and France
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Friday, October thirtieth. It's narrated by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.
In Italy, France 24 reports teen rallies take to the streets across Italy, reported so far by one source.
In South Africa, News24 reports March and March rejects arson claims and demands an end to online asylum registration, reported so far by one source.

In India, the Deccan Chronicle and Outlook report the Cockroach Janta Party announced its support for the opposition INDIA bloc's scheduled November first rally over alleged voter deletions, confirmed by independent reports.

In Albania, The Guardian reports the government adopted legislative measures imposing fines of up to 500,000 leks for individuals who remain in a crowd where violence occurs, reported so far by one source.
In Canada, CTV News declares British Columbia's Conservative Party wins a majority government in the snap election called for October twenty-fourth, confirmed by independent reports.
In France, the interior ministry says 410,000 people protested nationwide in marches over the cost of living and the high-school movement, reported so far by one source.

Italy's student and cost-of-living protests saw teen rallies take to the streets across Italy, reported so far by one source. Italy held a fourth round of nationwide protests called by Movimento 17 Ottobre with marches in at least 10 cities, confirmed by independent reports. The full timeline, with every source, is on the story page.
South Africa's asylum ruling unrest involves March and March rejecting arson claims, reported so far by one source. Coming up: local government elections on November fourth.

The Cockroach Janta Party movement announced its support for the opposition INDIA bloc's scheduled November first rally demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, confirmed by independent reports. UN human rights experts called on India to immediately stop using excessive force against protesters, confirmed by independent reports.

Albania's student protests follow government measures imposing fines for individuals remaining in violent crowds, reported so far by one source. The leaderless protest movement began peacefully in May against a luxury hotel project before morphing into anti-government protests, reported so far by one source.

Canada's Pacific Link pipeline fight concluded as British Columbia's Conservative Party won a majority government in the election called for October twenty-fourth, confirmed by independent reports. Leaders of six Métis nations say they were not consulted before Ottawa designated the pipeline, reported so far by one source.

France's high-school protests brought hundreds of thousands into the streets over the cost of living, reported so far by one source. Remnants of the gilets jaunes movement joined the protests and announced a further protest for October thirty-first, reported so far by one source.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
